title: Check for a live audit UI before trusting a telemetry count
trigger: when DD telemetry looks empty or a hook's effect is missing from the store, or when measuring retrieval events, cap_saturation or activation counts
behavior_delta: Check whether an audit UI is listening on the port in .dd/ui.json before concluding the hooks never ran. callRunningStore routes session-start, prompt and pre-tool to any live UI, which writes telemetry to that process's own data directory; the hook exits 0 and prints the bridged response either way, so nothing distinguishes a bridged call from a local one.
what: Check whether an audit UI is listening on the port in .dd/ui.json before concluding the hooks never ran. callRunningStore routes session-start, prompt and pre-tool to any live UI, which writes telemetry to that process's own data directory; the hook exits 0 and prints the bridged response either way, so nothing distinguishes a bridged call from a local one.
why: A stale audit UI from an older build silently absorbed every hook call while the current store stayed at zero retrieval events. The empty count reads as 'retrieval never ran' when the real cause is that another process answered.

revisit_when.description: The bridge gains a marker distinguishing a bridged response from a local one

evidence_refs.summary: callRunningStore posts session-start, prompt and pre-tool to the URL in .dd/ui.json and returns the response
if (bridged) ok(bridged) short-circuits before openStore, so the local store is never touched

legacy_reason: The per-project audit UI registered in .dd/ui.json was replaced by one resident per machine, found through ~/.dd-data/resident.json. callRunningStore now sends the project's data_dir and ignores a resident from an incompatible build, so another process no longer silently absorbs telemetry into its own data directory.
